sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 15.11.2019 at about 3.00 p.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 and when they reached near Thayaluru SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4124/2020 cross, NH75 road,
Mulbagal town, Kolar, at that time, the rider of the said Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 ridden the same in a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the opposite passing car bearing Reg.No.KA53MC4335.
Due to the said accident, Petitioner was fell down and had sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to R.L. Jalappa hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

The Petitioner had spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Carpenter and was earning Rs.600/ per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, he lost his income and also unable to do his work.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the Honda SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4124/2020 Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 by its rider.

The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R 3457 and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.2 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.1 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in its Written statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.

Further it contended that, SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4124/2020 the policy No. OG204404180600000067 valid from 29.07.2019 to 28.07.2020 in respect of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 is Liability only policy and the risk of the pillion rider and own damages claim does not cover as insured has not paid the extra premium to cover the risk of the pillion rider and it is covered only third party claims and the insurer of the said vehicle.
Further contended that the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and there is no rash or negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

sentences.text: On the rival Pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4124/2020 riding of Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA 53R 3457 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves that the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 8 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

8. The learned counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied on the following decision:
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4124/2020 1. MFA No.6621/2018 c/w MFA No.174/2018, between The National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs Sri Sanaulla Khan & others.

9. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 by its rider.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the offending Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 by its rider.
12. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 8 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.

Ex.P.1 to 8 are the FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet,
Statements and Aadhaar card.

13. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P.1 and 2 are the True copies of the FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Indushree, the Mulbagal Town Police have registered the case against the rider of the offending Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53 R3457 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4124/2020 Ex.P3 is the Spot mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
ExP4 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P5 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Mulbagal Town Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
14.
P.W.1 has been crossexamined by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 examined its Senior Executive by name Ruchitha Renukesh as RW.1 and got marked Authoirsation letter and Copy of Policy at Ex.R1 and 2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the Petitioner.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4124/2020 has proved the rash and negligent riding of the offending Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457 by its rider and due to the said accident, he had sustained injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15.
Issue No. 2 and 3: Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are inter linked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. It is stated in the petition that, the Petitioner is aged 26 years at the time of accident.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhar card at Ex.P8, which shows his date of birth was 09.07.1994.
The accident has taken place on 15.11.2019.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 26 years.

sentences.text: It is established that the Petitioner had suffered from injury in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The Petitioner has contended that he had sustained grievous injury and he has spent Rs.3,00,000/ for his medical treatment and other incidental charges.
But, Petitioner has not produced Wound Certificate or Discharge summary and any Medical bills.
18. The Petitioner did not choose to examine the doctor.
Apart from this, the Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards treatment as contended in the petition.
19. Though the Petitioner has averred that he has become unable to do his work because of the injury sustained by him, no Physical Disability Certificate has been produced.
The Petitioner has also not produced the Wound certificate to show what was the injuries sustained by him.
But, the Charge sheet SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4124/2020 shows he has sustained injuries to his left leg and head injury.
Hence, by considering the injuries, pain and suffering, food and nourishment and conveyance, it would be lawful to award global compensation of Rs.15,000/ to the Petitioner.

20. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending Honda Twister bearing Reg.No.KA53R3457.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
It is the contention taken by the Respondent No.2 that the Policy issued is Liability only Policy and it does not cover the risk of pillion rider and own damages.
The owner of the offending vehicle has not paid the extra premium to cover the risk of the pillion rider.
The Respondent No.1 got marked the Copy of Policy at Ex.R2 through RW.1.
Upon going through the same, it shows that the premium paid SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4124/2020 to the Basic 3rd Party Liability.

The Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied on the Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.1742018 (MVD) c/w MFA No.6621/2018 (MVD) in dated 24.11.2023, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to referred various decisions and observed that the "the petitioners are not the persons covered under the Motor Vehicles Act, as the decisions referred supra clearly and categorically lay down that the pillion rider being the gratuitous passenger is not a third party.
Therefore, the said clause is not at all applicable to the case on hand.

Hence, the contention of pay and recover is also not maintainable."
21.
In the present case also the owner of the offending motorcycle has not paid extra premium to cover the risk of pillion rider.
Moreover, the Respondent No.2 did not appear before the Court and did not contest the matter.
Under such circumstances, the Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4124/2020 offending vehicle is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
22. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 to 3 , I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.15,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4124/2020 date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the owner of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
